newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher, funds on both sides.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher, funds on both sides.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended a choppy session on the plus side as funds switched gears and turned technical buyers late, traders said.

"We had too big of a break in this market in the last few days," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities. "From the demand standpoint, we're still showing that we have tight stocks and you're going to see end-user coverage on any break like this."
Traders noted the May contract fell sharply in midday trading, triggering a buy signal in some trading programs used by commodity funds.
"Last week's low in the May beans was $8.16. We took that out and then Rosenthal Collins and Cargill started buying," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Nearby contracts were pressured most of the session by weak export and processing demand, highlighted by recent news several Cargill Inc crushers would take down-time this summer and rumors two other major processors were also cutting down.
Cutbacks will hurt nearby futures that had been bolstered by a 30 million bushel weekly crush pace, traders said.
Soybeans ended 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 3/4 cents lower with May up six at $8.31.

Cargill Inc on Friday said two more of its processing plants would take downtime this summer. The Kansas City and Norfolk, Va., crushers, along with a plant in Guntersville, Ala., will temporarily shut down because of falling crush margins and expensive soybeans.
The news confirmed a recent rally had priced domestic users out of the market and demand was not strong enough to entice them back in, traders.
World buyers were also turning away from pricey U.S. supplies. Taiwan will tender on Wednesday for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans but a buyer told Reuters Taiwan will not purchase U.S. soybeans.
"We will not consider U.S. soybeans because they are more than $10 higher than the South American grains," he said.

New crop months found strength from a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration report predicting the most widespread spring flooding in a decade. The report said heavy snow cover in the central and western sections of the country left the potential for flooding from snow melt.

On the day, Rosenthal Collins bought at least four million bushels May soybeans and two million bushels November, traders said. Refco Inc and SAK Futures each sold 4.5 million May. Griffin Trading sold three million May, sources said.
In options trade, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 May $7.75 puts at eight cents.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 81,010 contracts.
